ajinkya kawale Mumbai, 1 November The average daily value of Uniﬁed Payments Interface (UPI) transactions crossed ₹1 trillion for the ﬁrst time in Oc- tober, coinciding with the start of the festive season. The average daily volume stood at 822 million transactions dur- ing the month, also the high- est for UPI. October clocked 25.47 bil- lion transactions, around 23 per cent higher than the 20.7 billion transactions recorded in October 2025. Transactions worth ₹31.53 trillion were pro- cessed in October 2026, 16 per cent higher than the ₹27.27 tril- lion processed in October 2025. The focus on UPI’s volume and value comes at a time when a proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) is set to be levied on select person-to-mer- chant (P2M) transac- tions after Diwali. “The festive sea- son drove this rise. Navratri and the big online sales fell in October, and people used UPI for bigger festive purchases along with their everyday payments. From April to August, the number of UPI payments kept rising, but their daily value stayed ﬂat and the average payment kept get- ting smaller. In September and October, the value of payments grew faster than their number, and the average payment size went up for two months in a row,” said Reeju Datta, co- founder, Cashfree. In September, 24.06 billion transactions worth ₹29.37 trillion were processed. In Au- gust, 24.5 billion pay- ments amounting to ₹29.82 trillion were processed. Industry executives said the long-term sustainability of the payments system was criti- cal, especially during peak consumption periods such as the festive season. “The proposed Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) frame- work, initially scheduled for October 15 and reportedly de- ferred until after Diwali, brings an important question around the long-term sustainability of India’s digital payments infra- structure to the forefront. As transaction volumes rise dur- ing peak consumption periods, it is important to keep digital payments affordable for con- sumers and merchants while ensuring the ecosystem re- mains commercially sustain- able,” said Akshay Mehrotra, managing director and group chief executive officer, Fibe.
